PARTIAL-WORKING at HEAD (at-dock-convergence @ f8bde2f) — the four click sub-facilities each work but on FOUR uncoordinated mechanisms, and one is structurally absent. Concretely:

(1) CLICK-TO-EXPAND/PIN — WORKS, narrow path. `useDockState.onClickCollapsed()` flips state collapsed/hover → "pinned" (clears the idle timer; sticks until click-away). But it is wired to exactly ONE site: `GlassDock.vue:466` `@click="onClickCollapsed"` on the `.dock-layer--summary` pane, which only renders for `orientation === "horizontal"` collapsible docks (GlassDock.vue:450 `v-if`). A vertical/rail/always-expanded/instrument-strip dock has NO collapsed summary layer, so there is no click-to-pin affordance there at all (those are alwaysExpanded by contract, so it's moot — but the asymmetry is undocumented). Touch path is separate: `onTouchEnd` (GlassDock.vue:384) calls `expand()` (→ "hover", NOT "pinned") on a resolved tap, deliberately NOT preventing the native compatibility click (shape B′, the iOS Now-Playing single-tap contract). So mouse-click-on-collapsed → PINNED, tap-on-collapsed → HOVER. That state-divergence between click and tap is real and unspecified.

(2) CLICK-DRIVEN LAYER SWITCH — WORKS, two divergent idioms. The DockLayerGroup rail is a reka-ui Tabs contract: clicking a `role="tab"` writes the `active` v-model → fires `useLayerTransition` crossfade (DockLayerGroup.vue:143-173). The drill-in pattern (demo dock-layers.vue) instead hand-rolls plain `@click="open(id)"` buttons writing the same v-model. Both reach the same transition, but the layer-swap morph and the outer collapse morph run on TWO independent `useLayerTransition` engines (GlassDock.vue:253 outer + DockLayerGroup.vue:57 inner) — this is exactly the W02 born-RED two-clock defect: a click that simultaneously switches a layer AND collapses double-animates the same pixels on separate springs.

(3) ARIA-EXPANDED TRIGGER CONTRACT — CORRECT-BUT-CONSUMER-DEPENDENT. The dock root is deliberately presentational (`<div class="glass-dock">`, no role, no aria-expanded — GlassDock.vue:414-441) — putting aria-expanded there trips axe's aria-allowed-attr (AM.W0.2 gap 3). The contract is: consumer binds `:aria-expanded` to THEIR trigger button reading the dock's exposed `expanded` (defineExpose, GlassDock.vue:410). README best-practice #3 + CLAUDE.md document it. BUT: there is NO first-party trigger component and NO demo wiring `:aria-expanded` to a trigger — the only "trigger" in the live demo is the collapsed-summary slot itself, which carries no aria-expanded. So the contract is documented but unproven/unexemplified, and a collapsible-dock consumer following the docs has no reference implementation.

(4) SELECT/DROPDOWN TRIGGERS IN A DOCK — WORKS, well-wired. `DockSelectTrigger`/`DockDropdownTrigger` (thin reka SelectTrigger/DropdownMenuTrigger wrappers) compose inside the dock; the critical click-away seam is intact: `SelectContent`/`DropdownMenuContent`/`PopoverContent`/`HoverPopover` all stamp `data-glass-dock-portal` + `data-glass-dock-owner=<dockId>` from the injected dock context, and `isTeleportedTarget()` + `useDockState.onPointerDownOutside`/`onMouseLeave`/`onFocusOut` all treat a click/focus inside that teleported overlay as "inside the dock" so the dock does not collapse while a menu is open. This is the keyframes-D9 "menu-dropped-out-of-keepOpen" break, already closed. Note `DockSelectTrigger` deliberately does NOT hover-scale (anchors the popup), `DockDropdownTrigger` DOES — a documented divergence.

THE GESTURE (paired-π BEFORE/AFTER/DELTA over ≥3 viewports): `page.hover` to expand the dock → real `pointerdown` on the `data-slot='slider'` thumb → real drag → `pointerleave` the dock → HOLD past the 600ms collapse delay (sample at ~900ms) → release.

APPEARANCE axis (frontend-design sign-off): (1) the dock substrate `.glass-dock[data-held]` tier-shades up (resting→floating background + quieted border) and DOES NOT idle-collapse while held; (2) the thumb halo `.glass-slider[data-held]` intensifies to the denser surface-tint rung (`0 0 0 8px var(--surface-tint-15)`); halo is centered on the circular knob, no detached ring, no occlusion.

INTERACTION axis: the held visual applies IMMEDIATELY on pointerdown (instant-on, under ~100ms perception threshold — NO spring lag arming the halo); the value tracks the drag continuously (iOS continuous-knob feel).

INTERRUPTION axis: release re-arms the idle timer — the dock collapses AFTER, not DURING, the drag; AND a `pointercancel`-injected mid-drag arm clears `data-held` (no permanent hold); AND a multi-slider arm (story 3) proves ref-count (release one of two, dock stays held).

PRM axis: with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` emulated, the dock STILL HOLDS open under the held drag (function preserved) while the settle motion is damped (PRM kills motion, not the hold).

TOUCH parity: a touch-emulated drag (Chrome DevTools touch emulation) holds identically through one single acquire path.
